ideas.idea: Commander's intent and mission tactics: state the task and its purpose, prescribe method only as far as coordination needs, against cascading KPIs that prescribe outputs
Subordinates should understand intent two levels up
Friction and uncertainty are the normal condition; plans that assume otherwise deny the nature of the work
No zero-defects mentality: be lenient on bold errors and severe on inaction, against appraisal systems that punish visible mistakes
Deference to expertise and a reluctance to simplify: decisions migrate to whoever knows most, not to rank
Preoccupation with failure: treat weak signals and near-misses as data, against dashboards that report green
Normalization of deviance and schedule pressure: a success record is not evidence of safety; Columbia's foam
An independent technical authority or safety function with its own line, not one that reports to the programme it checks
Work as imagined versus work as done; learn why the action made sense at the time, not who broke the rule
The after-action review: leaders enter the discussion only when necessary, it is permissible to disagree, no critique or lecture
What the textbooks teach that the doctrine contradicts: management by objectives and goal cascades; control systems; change managed through a programme
A disagreement among the doctrine sources: the war-fighting doctrine prizes tempo, boldness and accepting risk; the high-reliability sources prize redundancy, verification and stopping when unsure
Simple, complicated, complex: the playbook fits the complicated case and fails in the complex one

note: All 103 marker occurrences graded. The 'how did the organization fail...' quotes swap 'worker' for the source's 'individual' (no). The third MISSING entry is a locator mis-pair on a one-word quote, not graded. Failures: the Main Effort chunk [19] carries none of it; the burden-of-proof chunk [30] is cited for middle managers shielding executives; 'zero-tolerance for unapproved procedural deviations' overstates DOE, whose zero tolerance is for reckless violations. Steering-committee claims overreach their chunks, and DOE HPI is cited as 'Textbook Doctrine'.
